scope: Targeted source and equation review for morphology and mechanical-load sensitivity. No full-paper scholarly review or lunar empirical validation claimed.
external_bytes: No external papers or datasets added to the repository. Web text extraction supplied the cited passages; binary downloads to /tmp failed because command-line DNS was unavailable, so no raw-source byte hashes are claimed.

sources.authors: Robin J. Hogan, Lin Tian, Philip R. A. Brown, Christopher D. Westbrook, Andrew J. Heymsfield and Jon D. Eastment
sources.title: Radar Scattering from Ice Aggregates Using the Horizontally Aligned Oblate Spheroid Approximation
sources.publication: Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology 51, 655–671 (2012)
sources.reading_extent: Abstract; section 2 mass/dimension conventions and equation 4; discussion of aircraft/radar consistency and scope. Publisher view returned 403; author-hosted published PDF text was retrieved.
sources.use: Brown–Francis uses mean orthogonal image dimension. Dmax approximately 1.25 Dmean gives m=0.0121 Dmax^1.9 in SI; holding 0.0185 while calling D maximum introduces a convention error.
sources.limit: Earth ice-cloud closure; no validation of 15–60 cm aggregates. The study itself reports remaining disagreement between mass fits to radar and water content.

sources.authors: Axel Seifert, Fabian Jakub, Christoph Siewert, Leonie von Terzi and Stefan Kneifel
sources.title: On the geometry of aggregate snowflakes
sources.reading_extent: Abstract; sections 2, 3.1–3.4 and initial section 4.1; equations 1–26 and their definitions. Geometry pictures were not visually inspected.
sources.use: Needle, plate and dendrite aggregate geometry; q normalizes projected area by an ellipse, while phi gives horizontal aspect ratio. The circle-normalized area is q*phi. habits.py implements mean phi/q fits from equations 9–17.
sources.limit: Synthetic unrimed aggregate geometries, 2–2048 monomers and mean input monomer sizes 50–500 micrometres. Holding representative q*phi constant at all population sizes is our sensitivity assumption. Multiplying fitted means does not reproduce the joint distribution. This paper is by Seifert et al.; Leinonen's earlier aggregation model underlies it.

sources.title: Toward a Comprehensive Model of Snow Crystal Growth Dynamics: 1. Overarching Features and Physical Origins
sources.reading_extent: Introduction, Figure 1 caption and physical discussion of temperature, supersaturation, pressure and morphology; extracted PDF text. Diagram screenshot retrieval failed, so no boundaries were digitized.
sources.use: Growth-form anchors near -2, -5, -7 and -15 C and greater morphological complexity with increased supersaturation. Only temperature anchors are mapped into the lunar column.
sources.limit: Atmospheric-pressure laboratory context and a partly semi-empirical growth model; lunar cloud history, nucleation, fractions of habits and individual crystal shape remain unpredicted.

sources.authors: Christopher D. Westbrook, Robin J. Hogan and Anthony J. Illingworth
sources.title: The Capacitance of Pristine Ice Crystals and Aggregate Snowflakes
sources.reading_extent: Publisher abstract and aggregate-capacitance results surrounding Figures 13–14; preprint abstract independently checked.
sources.use: Aggregate capacitance C/Dmax approximately 0.25, with shape dependence; retained existing closure for controlled geometry comparisons.
sources.limit: Diffusional capacitance, not optical cross section or mechanical strength. The earlier geometric model's circle-area ratios span a wider range than the newer Seifert representative families.

sources.authors: Pierre Grzegorczyk, Sudha Yadav, Florian Zanger, Alexander Theis, Subir K. Mitra, Stephan Borrmann and Miklos Szakall
sources.title: Fragmentation of ice particles: laboratory experiments on graupel–graupel and graupel–snowflake collisions
sources.publication: Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 23, 13505–13521 (2023), with 2024 corrigendum
sources.reading_extent: Abstract, experimental description, snowflake results including no-collision blank measurements; corrigendum text inspected for area convention.
sources.use: Artificial 10 mm dendritic aggregates shed monomers or branches on release even without collision. Contact network and baseline aerodynamic loading matter in addition to ambient turbulent velocity differences.
sources.limit: Artificial Earth-gravity particles and release procedure; fragment counts do not calibrate lunar decimetre flake strength. The corrigendum addresses the area convention of fitted breakup coefficients; those coefficients are not imported here.

sources.authors: Hassan Bahaloo, Tobias Eidevag, Per Gren, Johan Casselgren, Fredrik Forsberg, Per Abrahamsson and Mikael Sjodahl
sources.title: Ice sintering: Dependence of sintering force on temperature, load, duration, and particle size
sources.reading_extent: Institutional published-PDF abstract and introduction; publisher indexed methods and results excerpts. Direct publisher full-text retrieval failed.
sources.use: Ice-contact strength depends on temperature, contact load, contact duration and particle size. Longer residence may change bonds, while sublimation may erode them.
sources.limit: Loaded ice contacts do not supply the unknown connectivity, contact history or failure capacity of a freely suspended snow aggregate. No numerical strength transferred to the lunar snow model.

unadmitted_sources.title: A Taxonomy of Snow Crystal Growth Behaviors: 2. Quantifying the Nakaya Diagram
unadmitted_sources.status: Abstract identified; HTML unavailable and PDF too large for web retrieval. The 206-image dataset was not inspected, digitized or used as model input.
